nodes.label: Bottom-up Attentional Capture
nodes.definition: Priority allocation toward salient or otherwise attention-attracting events that can occur even when those events are not aligned with the current task goal.
exclusions: learned selection-history effects when those are the primary mechanism
nodes.mechanism_summary: Competition for attentional priority can favor salient events; control depends on interaction with goals and selection history.
failure_modes: Treating salience as sufficient for guaranteed attention
Assuming capture is fully independent of goals/context
open_questions: Operational boundary with novelty orienting and selection-history capture

nodes.label: Working-Memory Capacity
nodes.definition: Limited capacity for maintaining and using currently relevant information under task demands.
inclusions: capacity constraints relevant to active processing
nodes.mechanism_summary: Working-memory limitations constrain active representation and interact with attentional control.
failure_modes: Equating one task score with universal capacity
Treating capacity as identical to cognitive load
open_questions: Task-general versus task-specific capacity modeling

nodes.label: Expectancy of Success
nodes.definition: A person's expectation or belief about the likelihood of succeeding at a task or attaining a goal.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Expectancy contributes to motivational choice, effort or persistence in combination with value and context.
failure_modes: Treating expectancy as value
Assuming high expectancy always increases action regardless of value/cost
open_questions: Boundary with self-efficacy and perceived control

nodes.label: Goal-Relevance Appraisal
nodes.definition: Evaluation of whether an event or situation bears on the person's goals, concerns, or well-being.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Appraisal of personal significance contributes to emotional differentiation and action tendencies.
failure_modes: Using emotional label as proof of the underlying appraisal
Confusing goal relevance with positive valence
open_questions: Interaction with novelty, controllability and certainty appraisals

nodes.label: Group Identification
nodes.definition: The degree to which a group membership is psychologically incorporated into the self and becomes relevant to perception and behavior.
inclusions: strength of identification with a group
nodes.mechanism_summary: Identification can change the relevance of group norms and referent influence.
failure_modes: Inferring strong identification from membership alone
Treating all group effects as identity effects
open_questions: State versus chronic identification in commercial contexts

nodes.label: Injunctive Norm
nodes.definition: A perceived or communicated socially shared view about what people should or should not do.
exclusions: formal legal rule unless socially represented as a norm
nodes.mechanism_summary: Injunctive norms can guide behavior through internalization or anticipated social enforcement, with important reactance/autonomy boundaries.
failure_modes: Confusing what others do with what others approve
Assuming norm messaging cannot backfire
open_questions: Conditions producing reactance or undermining intrinsic motivation

nodes.label: Risk Perception
nodes.definition: Subjective judgment about the possibility and/or severity of uncertain adverse outcomes.
exclusions: probability weighting as a specific mechanism
nodes.mechanism_summary: Risk perception contributes to judgment under uncertainty but is analytically distinct from preference and final choice.
failure_modes: Equating perceived risk with objective probability
Inferring risk aversion from high risk perception
open_questions: Decomposition into likelihood versus severity across domains

nodes.label: Attribute Trade-Off Conflict
nodes.definition: Conflict arising when alternatives differ on attributes or goals such that improvement on one dimension requires sacrifice on another.
exclusions: simple preference with no competing attributes
opportunity cost awareness as a separate process
nodes.mechanism_summary: Trade-off structure shapes whether decision makers balance attributes, choose compromise options, or adopt more extreme solutions.
failure_modes: Treating all multiattribute choice as experienced conflict
Assuming a single universal compromise response
open_questions: Moderators of mixed versus extreme resolution

nodes.label: Attitudinal Ambivalence
nodes.definition: Coexistence of positive and negative evaluative tendencies toward the same attitude object.
exclusions: uncertainty caused only by lack of knowledge
neutral attitude with no positive or negative evaluation
nodes.mechanism_summary: Ambivalence is an attitude-structure property that can affect certainty, processing and resistance.
failure_modes: Equating ambivalence with neutrality
Equating ambivalence with low confidence
open_questions: Objective versus subjective ambivalence and their runtime relevance

nodes.label: Attitude–Behavior Consistency
nodes.definition: The degree to which an attitude corresponds with or predicts relevant behavior under specified conditions.
exclusions: mere attitude strength without behavioral observation
nodes.mechanism_summary: Attitudes do not map mechanically to behavior; context, self-interest, control and other moderators can affect consistency.
failure_modes: Using attitude change as proof of behavioral change
Substituting intention for observed behavior
open_questions: Which moderators are most useful for copywriting runtime inference

nodes.label: Common Ground
nodes.definition: Information that communicators treat as shared background for the purposes of their interaction.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Language interpretation and audience design can depend on what information is treated as shared, using mechanisms whose efficiency varies with context and cognitive demands.
failure_modes: Assuming the audience actually shares what the writer presupposes
Equating common ground with demographic similarity
open_questions: How to infer common ground safely from customer research

nodes.label: Situation-Model Construction
nodes.definition: Construction of a mental representation of the situation described by discourse, beyond the surface wording and local propositions.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Comprehenders integrate discourse and knowledge into a representation that supports coherence and inference.
failure_modes: Assuming comprehension from surface recall alone
Treating situation models as directly observable without task-specific inference
open_questions: Best operational proxies for commercial message comprehension

nodes.label: Narrative Transportation
nodes.definition: A state in which a recipient becomes mentally immersed in the world evoked by a narrative.
inclusions: narrative immersion as operationalized in transportation research
nodes.mechanism_summary: Transportation is a narrative-processing construct with empirically studied antecedents, moderators and persuasive consequences.
failure_modes: Equating engagement metrics with transportation
Assuming every story transports every audience
open_questions: Channel and audience moderators relevant to copy runtime

nodes.label: Refutational Two-Sided Message
nodes.definition: A persuasive message that acknowledges opposing considerations and explicitly refutes or answers them.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Message-sidedness effects depend on whether opposing arguments are refuted and on message/context characteristics.
failure_modes: Assuming two-sidedness is universally more persuasive
Treating concession without refutation as equivalent
open_questions: Boundary conditions by product category, audience position and time pressure

nodes.label: Processing Fluency
nodes.definition: The subjective ease with which information is processed.
exclusions: mere familiarity as a cause rather than the fluency experience
nodes.mechanism_summary: Fluency can inform judgment through affective or interpretive pathways; meaning depends on context and attribution.
failure_modes: Assuming fluent means true or good
Equating readability with fluency
Equating fluency with comprehension
open_questions: Perceptual versus conceptual subtypes and copy-specific moderators

nodes.label: Autonomous Motivation
nodes.definition: Motivation experienced with a sense of willingness, volition and personal endorsement, including intrinsic motivation and sufficiently internalized extrinsic motivation.
inclusions: identified/integrated forms of extrinsic regulation when genuinely endorsed
nodes.mechanism_summary: The quality/source of regulation differs from motivation amount and can affect persistence and experience.
failure_modes: Treating autonomy as absence of external context
Equating autonomous with intrinsic only
open_questions: Transport from work/education to consumer action contexts

nodes.label: Controlled Motivation
nodes.definition: Motivation regulated by external or internal pressure, contingencies, demands or controlling reasons rather than full personal endorsement.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Controlled regulation can produce action while differing functionally from autonomous motivation.
failure_modes: Equating controlled motivation with extrinsic motivation universally
Assuming controlled motivation cannot produce behavior
open_questions: Conditions under which persuasive pressure shifts autonomous to controlled regulation

nodes.label: Descriptive Norm
nodes.definition: A perception or communication about what relevant others typically do.
exclusions: simple popularity without a relevant social referent
nodes.mechanism_summary: Descriptive norms provide social information about common behavior and can differ from injunctive expectations.
failure_modes: Confusing prevalence with approval
Treating platform popularity as a validated norm measure
open_questions: Referent proximity and domain moderators

nodes.label: Reference Point
nodes.definition: A comparison standard relative to which outcomes or changes in value are evaluated.
exclusions: anchor used only for numeric estimation
objective baseline with no psychological comparison role
nodes.mechanism_summary: Reference-dependent evaluation can change sensitivity to gains/losses or changes relative to a comparison standard.
failure_modes: Assuming the status quo is always the operative reference
Assuming a single reference point
open_questions: How multiple reference points are selected in commercial choice

nodes.label: Loss Aversion
nodes.definition: Greater sensitivity to losses than comparable gains relative to an operative reference point.
inclusions: loss-gain asymmetry conditional on reference point
nodes.mechanism_summary: Loss aversion is one possible reference-dependent asymmetry; robustness and generality vary by paradigm and reference-point structure.
failure_modes: Treating loss aversion as a universal law
Explaining every negative framing effect as loss aversion
open_questions: Domain robustness and reference-point moderators

nodes.label: Perceived Source Expertise
nodes.definition: Perceived competence or ability of a source to provide valid information within the relevant domain.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Expertise is a source-credibility dimension whose persuasive impact depends on receiver/message/context conditions.
failure_modes: Treating credentials as guaranteed perceived expertise
Assuming expertise always increases persuasion
open_questions: Interaction with prior attitudes and elaboration

nodes.label: Perceived Source Trustworthiness
nodes.definition: Perceived honesty, integrity or lack of deceptive intent attributed to a source in the relevant communication context.
exclusions: relational trust as a broad interpersonal history unless source evaluation is the target
nodes.mechanism_summary: Trustworthiness is a distinct source-credibility dimension and its effect is context-dependent.
failure_modes: Equating trustworthiness with expertise
Assuming familiar/liked sources are necessarily trustworthy
open_questions: Interaction with transparency and persuasion knowledge

nodes.label: Metaphor Comprehension
nodes.definition: Processes by which a listener or reader derives intended figurative meaning from metaphorical expressions.
exclusions: analogy used purely as argumentative structure
nodes.mechanism_summary: Multiple theoretical accounts—analogy, categorization and conceptual mapping—capture aspects of metaphor comprehension; no single mechanism is assumed universally.
failure_modes: Treating every metaphor as conceptual mapping only
Assuming figurative language improves comprehension by default
open_questions: Familiarity, novelty and complexity moderators

nodes.label: Two-Sided Message
nodes.definition: A persuasive message structure that presents both supporting and opposing or negative considerations about the advocated position/object.
exclusions: simple disclaimer unrelated to the advocated claim
nodes.mechanism_summary: Two-sidedness is a structural property; persuasive effects depend on refutation, amount/placement of negative information and receiver/context characteristics.
failure_modes: Assuming two-sided messages are universally superior
Equating any caveat with substantive two-sidedness
open_questions: Optimal use across sophistication/knowledge states and channels

nodes.label: Perceptual Salience
nodes.definition: Relative perceptual prominence of a stimulus feature or object that can bias selection priority.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Perceptual prominence contributes to competition for selection but does not guarantee capture.
failure_modes: Equating salience with actual attention
Inferring salience from engagement outcomes
open_questions: Cross-modal and naturalistic-copy salience

nodes.label: Attentional Set / Target Template
nodes.definition: An active representation of goal-relevant target properties that biases selective attention.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Goal-relevant representations alter competition for attentional selection.
failure_modes: Assuming a marketing persona proves an attentional set
open_questions: Naturalistic inference from search intent and task context

nodes.label: Executive Attentional Control
nodes.definition: Control processes that regulate attentional competition in accordance with task goals.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Executive control can bias selection and resolve interference while interacting with working-memory representations.
failure_modes: Treating one reaction-time score as global executive control
open_questions: Task-specific transport

nodes.label: Reward-Associated Attentional Priority
nodes.definition: Attentional priority acquired through prior associations between features and reward or learned value.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Learning history can persistently bias later selection, but magnitude is method-sensitive.
failure_modes: Using prior likes as direct evidence of value-driven capture
Assigning a universal effect coefficient
open_questions: Transport from visual-search paradigms to copy exposure

nodes.label: Prior-Selection History
nodes.definition: Bias in current attentional priority attributable to prior selections independently of current goals or physical salience.
exclusions: reward learning when reward association is the primary mechanism
nodes.mechanism_summary: Past selection episodes can alter future priority.
failure_modes: Failing to control current goals/salience
open_questions: Duration and context specificity

nodes.label: Sustained Attention
nodes.definition: Maintenance of task-relevant attentional engagement over an extended interval.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Sustained attention concerns ongoing task-relevant processing rather than initial selection.
failure_modes: Inferring sustained attention from early hold or completion rate alone
open_questions: Naturalistic content-specific measurement

nodes.label: Vigilance Decrement
nodes.definition: Decline in performance or attentional maintenance as time-on-task increases under vigilance demands.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Performance may degrade over sustained monitoring time.
failure_modes: Calling any drop-off a vigilance decrement without task controls
open_questions: Applicability to media consumption

nodes.label: Attentional Disengagement
nodes.definition: Process of releasing or shifting attentional priority away from the currently selected target.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Disengagement governs release from current priority and can shape switching/reorientation.
failure_modes: Equating disengagement with suppression
open_questions: Naturalistic message transition effects

nodes.label: Certainty Appraisal
nodes.definition: Appraisal of how certain or predictable an event, cause, or outcome appears within an emotional episode.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Certainty appraisal contributes to differentiated emotional response patterns.
failure_modes: Confusing emotional certainty appraisal with epistemic confidence
open_questions: Commercial threat/opportunity contexts

nodes.label: Controllability / Coping-Potential Appraisal
nodes.definition: Appraisal of whether and how a person can control, cope with, or respond effectively to an event or its consequences.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Perceived control and coping potential contribute to emotion differentiation and action tendency.
failure_modes: Assuming objective control equals perceived control
open_questions: Interaction with fear/anger/hope in copy

nodes.label: Affective Arousal
nodes.definition: Degree of affective activation or energetic intensity, analytically separable from positive-negative valence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Arousal can alter readiness and, in some contexts, social transmission, but its meaning depends on appraisal and context.
failure_modes: Inferring emotion identity from arousal
Assuming high arousal guarantees sharing/action
open_questions: Channel and audience moderators

nodes.label: Approach Action Tendency
nodes.definition: Readiness or tendency to move toward, engage with, acquire, confront, or otherwise act in an approach-oriented direction.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Appraisal and affect can organize approach-oriented action readiness, but valence does not map one-to-one onto approach.
failure_modes: Equating positive affect with approach
open_questions: Distinct approach forms in commercial decisions

nodes.label: Withdrawal / Avoidance Action Tendency
nodes.definition: Readiness or tendency to withdraw from, avoid, escape, or disengage from a target or situation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Appraisal and affect can organize withdrawal/avoidance readiness, but negative valence does not map one-to-one onto avoidance.
failure_modes: Equating negative affect with avoidance
open_questions: Threat versus disgust versus effort-based avoidance

nodes.label: Self-Relevance
nodes.definition: Degree to which information, outcomes, or identities connect to a personally important aspect of the self.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Self-relevance can alter valuation, attention and processing by linking information to self-representations.
failure_modes: Inferring self-relevance from demographic targeting alone
open_questions: State versus chronic self-relevance

nodes.label: Self-Categorization
nodes.definition: Psychological classification of self as a member of a salient social category, affecting self-perception and social influence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Salient self-categorization can make group norms and prototypes self-relevant.
failure_modes: Inferring self-categorization from membership only
open_questions: Contextual activation in market segments

nodes.label: In-Group Prototypicality
nodes.definition: Degree to which a person, source, or position is perceived as representative of a salient in-group.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Prototypicality can shape who is influential when a group identity is salient.
failure_modes: Using surface similarity as proof of prototypicality
open_questions: Source prototypicality versus product prototypicality

nodes.label: Perceived Source Genuineness / Authenticity
nodes.definition: Perception that a source's self-presentation or communication is genuine rather than fabricated or strategically false in a way relevant to evaluation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Genuineness can contribute to source evaluation, especially in relational or influencer contexts, with contextual heterogeneity.
failure_modes: Treating casual tone as authenticity
Equating authenticity with factual accuracy
open_questions: Transport beyond creator/influencer contexts

nodes.label: Source Reliability Track Record
nodes.definition: Historical evidence or perception that a source has produced dependable outcomes or accurate/reliable information over time.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Past reliability can inform source evaluation but is domain-specific and evidence for an independent stable construct is not yet sufficient here.
failure_modes: Treating past reliability as guaranteed current accuracy
open_questions: Best construct placement versus evidence-traceability module

nodes.label: Attentional Encoding
nodes.definition: Encoding of information into memory under selective attentional allocation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Attention at encoding changes which information is available for later memory; later recall/recognition additionally depends on retrieval processes.
failure_modes: Treating exposure as encoding
Treating recall failure as proof of no attention

nodes.label: Active Goal Representation
nodes.definition: A currently relevant desired state or outcome represented as an organizing target for cognition and action.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Active goals organize attention, valuation, effort and self-regulation.
failure_modes: Inferring active goals solely from demographics

nodes.label: Promotion Focus
nodes.definition: Regulatory orientation centered on advancement, growth and accomplishment.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Promotion-focused concerns change sensitivity to advancement/gain-relevant means and can interact with message framing/fit.
failure_modes: Equating promotion focus with positive mood
Assuming regulatory fit always improves objective decision quality

nodes.label: Affective Forecasting
nodes.definition: Prediction of one's future emotional response to a prospective event, decision, or outcome.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Predicted future feelings can guide decisions, but forecasts can be biased and are distinct from current affect.
failure_modes: Equating anticipated affect with current affect
Assuming forecasts are accurate

nodes.label: Goal Persistence
nodes.definition: Continued allocation of effort and action toward a goal across time or obstacles.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Persistence is a central self-regulatory process, but adaptive regulation can also require disengagement.
failure_modes: Treating persistence as universally adaptive

nodes.label: Impression Management
nodes.definition: Attempts to influence the impressions that others form about the self or actor.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Self-presentation tactics can shape social evaluation but vary by tactic, audience and context.
failure_modes: Equating all self-presentation with deception

nodes.label: Compliance
nodes.definition: Behavioral change or action in response to a request or social influence attempt.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Compliance is request-linked social influence and differs from conformity to group behavior or norms.
failure_modes: Confusing compliance with agreement or attitude change

nodes.label: Reciprocity Norm
nodes.definition: Social expectation that benefits, concessions, or favorable treatment may call for an appropriate return.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Reciprocity can shape compliance and exchange but is conditional on context and perceived intent.
failure_modes: Treating gifts as automatic obligations
Ignoring manipulation recognition

nodes.label: Descriptive Consensus / Social-Proof Cue
nodes.definition: Applied social cue conveying that many relevant others endorse, choose, or attend to an option.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Consensus cues can inform social inference, but overlap with descriptive norms and source-credibility cues.
failure_modes: Equating popularity with truth
Duplicating descriptive norm as a new construct

nodes.label: Need to Belong
nodes.definition: Motivational need to establish and maintain meaningful social bonds and avoid exclusion.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Threats to belonging can produce compensatory relational or control-oriented responses.
failure_modes: Assuming every social action is belonging-driven

nodes.label: Recognition Heuristic
nodes.definition: A heuristic that can use recognition of one alternative and nonrecognition of another as a cue for inference under suitable environmental structures.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Simple heuristics can be adaptive when their cue structure matches the environment.
failure_modes: Treating recognition as always valid
Generalizing beyond environments where recognition correlates with criterion

nodes.label: Default Effect
nodes.definition: Change in choice probability produced by preselecting or designating one option as the default.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Defaults influence choice through multiple possible channels and exhibit substantial contextual heterogeneity.
failure_modes: Assuming defaults always increase uptake
Treating default effect size as universal

nodes.label: Temporal Discounting
nodes.definition: Reduction in the subjective value of outcomes as their delay increases.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Intertemporal valuation depends on delay and can display present bias and other time-related distortions.
failure_modes: Equating temporal discounting with impatience as a stable trait

nodes.label: Numeric Anchoring Effect
nodes.definition: Shift in a numerical judgment toward a previously encountered comparison value or anchor.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Anchors can strongly affect judgment but effects vary by relevance, dimension, incentives and debiasing.
failure_modes: Treating any first number as an effective anchor
Using meta-analytic average as a universal marketing coefficient

nodes.label: Effort Cost
nodes.definition: Subjective cost assigned to the effort required to obtain an outcome or complete an action.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Effort commonly discounts value but may also increase value under some conditions.
failure_modes: Assuming lower effort is always preferred

nodes.label: Message Elaboration Depth
nodes.definition: Degree of thoughtful cognitive processing devoted to the merits, implications, and arguments of a persuasive message.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Higher elaboration increases sensitivity to argument strength and changes the role of simpler cues.
failure_modes: Inferring elaboration solely from time spent
Treating central/peripheral as mutually exclusive fixed routes

nodes.label: Argument Strength / Quality
nodes.definition: Degree to which message arguments generate favorable versus unfavorable issue-relevant cognitive responses under a specified evaluative standard.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Strong-versus-weak argument effects are amplified under greater elaboration, but operationalization must be constructually explicit.
failure_modes: Labeling an argument strong because it won a pretest without analyzing why
Treating argument quality as context-free

nodes.label: Psychological Reactance
nodes.definition: Motivational-affective-cognitive response to a perceived threat to behavioral freedom.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Freedom-threatening messages can evoke anger and counterarguing that undermine persuasion.
failure_modes: Calling any disagreement reactance
Ignoring baseline freedom relevance

nodes.label: Attitude Certainty
nodes.definition: Subjective confidence in the correctness, clarity, or validity of one's attitude.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Certainty is an attitude-strength property that can affect persistence, resistance and behavior relations.
failure_modes: Equating certainty with extremity
Equating source confidence with attitude certainty

nodes.label: Claim Verifiability
nodes.definition: Degree to which a communicated claim can be checked against observable, traceable, or independently assessable evidence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Verifiability is operationally useful for proof architecture, but its psychological effects must be represented through evidence evaluation, trust and learning mechanisms rather than assumed directly.
failure_modes: Treating verifiability as truth
Assuming verifiable claims automatically persuade

nodes.label: Lexical Ambiguity / Polysemy
nodes.definition: Presence of multiple possible lexical senses or meanings requiring contextual resolution.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Lexical interpretation integrates word-level information with syntactic, semantic and discourse context.
failure_modes: Treating all ambiguity as stylistic creativity
Ignoring intended-audience lexical knowledge

nodes.label: Sentence Parsing Load
nodes.definition: Processing demand associated with constructing and revising syntactic structure during sentence comprehension.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Parsing depends on structural and lexical/contextual information under memory constraints.
failure_modes: Equating sentence length with parsing load

nodes.label: Presupposition
nodes.definition: Backgrounded proposition or content conventionally/pragmatically treated as already in the discourse context under particular linguistic triggers.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Presupposition interpretation interacts with discourse context, embedding and projection.
failure_modes: Assuming all readers accept a presupposition
Using presupposition to hide unsupported factual claims

nodes.label: Linguistic Predictability / Surprisal
nodes.definition: Degree to which upcoming linguistic material is expected given preceding context, with surprisal formalizing information associated with unexpected continuations.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Predictability can alter online processing difficulty, while formal surprisal models have empirical limits and should not be equated with curiosity.
failure_modes: Treating surprisal as attention or interest
Assuming unpredictability always improves copy

nodes.label: Information Structure / Focus
nodes.definition: Organization of utterance content according to what is at issue, foregrounded, given, new, focused, or backgrounded in discourse.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Interpretation of focus and projective content depends on discourse structure such as the current question under discussion.
failure_modes: Equating visual emphasis with linguistic focus

nodes.label: Claim–Support Argument Structure
nodes.definition: Rhetorical organization in which a claim is supported by reasons, evidence, or warrants that make the inferential relation inspectable.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Argument structure determines how support is organized, while receiver-side argument evaluation belongs primarily to C5.
failure_modes: Treating structure alone as sufficient for truth or persuasion

nodes.label: Emotional Appeal
nodes.definition: Deliberate message design intended to evoke or leverage emotion as part of persuasion.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Emotional appeals are heterogeneous by emotion and context; they feed C2 affect and C5 persuasion rather than constituting an emotion themselves.
failure_modes: Treating 'emotional' as one mechanism
Assuming emotional appeals universally outperform rational appeals

nodes.label: Information Sequence
nodes.definition: Deliberate ordering of claims, evidence, cues, disclosures, or other message elements over the course of communication.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Order can alter processing and later judgment in bounded settings, but no universal primacy/recency rule is accepted.
failure_modes: Applying primacy/recency as universal copy formulas

nodes.label: Comparative Message Structure
nodes.definition: Message architecture that explicitly or implicitly contrasts the advocated option with one or more alternatives.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Comparative structure can alter attention, processing and evaluation while creating possible source-believability trade-offs.
failure_modes: Assuming comparison always improves persuasion
Ignoring credibility/legal/factual constraints

nodes.label: Narrative Suspense
nodes.definition: Narrative tension characterized by anticipation about uncertain consequential outcomes.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Suspense can shape anticipation and immersion in narrative contexts; transport to nonnarrative copy remains uncertain.
failure_modes: Calling any unanswered question suspense
Assuming suspense improves conversion

nodes.label: Direct Action Request
nodes.definition: Explicit linguistic request for the recipient to perform a specified action.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Request presence and wording can influence compliance under some conditions, but CTA effectiveness depends on social, motivational and friction mechanisms.
failure_modes: Treating a CTA phrase as a universal conversion mechanism

nodes.label: Working-Memory Updating
nodes.definition: Control process that revises the contents of working memory by adding newly relevant information and removing or replacing no-longer-relevant contents.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Updating changes the actively maintained representation used for ongoing processing and action.
failure_modes: Equating updating with storage capacity
Inferring updating ability from one platform behavior

nodes.label: Cognitive Load
nodes.definition: Demand imposed by a task or representation on limited active processing resources.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Higher processing demand can consume resources needed for comprehension, maintenance, integration, or control.
failure_modes: Treating complexity as load without measuring task/person interaction
Equating load with working-memory capacity

nodes.label: Perceptual Fluency
nodes.definition: Experienced ease of processing the perceptual form of a stimulus.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Perceptual features can alter processing ease, which may then be interpreted in downstream judgments.
failure_modes: Equating visual simplicity with comprehension
Assuming fluent equals true

nodes.label: Conceptual Fluency
nodes.definition: Experienced ease of processing a stimulus's meaning, semantic relations, or conceptual interpretation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Semantic fit and prior conceptual activation can make meaning easier to process, with downstream judgment effects depending on attribution.
failure_modes: Equating conceptual fluency with factual understanding

nodes.label: Goal Commitment
nodes.definition: Degree of attachment to and determination to pursue a specified goal.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Commitment affects persistence and resource allocation but is distinct from importance, desirability, and attainability.
failure_modes: Assuming importance guarantees commitment

nodes.label: Prevention Focus
nodes.definition: Regulatory orientation emphasizing security, responsibilities, and avoiding losses or failures.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Prevention-focused concerns change sensitivity to vigilance, safety and loss-relevant means, often in contrast with promotion focus.
failure_modes: Equating prevention focus with fear
Assuming prevention framing always fits every risk-averse audience

nodes.label: Subjective Task Value
nodes.definition: Perceived importance, usefulness, interest, or worth associated with engaging in a task or attaining its outcome.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Value combines with expectancy and cost to shape motivation, choice, effort, and persistence.
failure_modes: Equating value with reward magnitude
Ignoring cost and expectancy

nodes.label: Anticipated Regret
nodes.definition: Prospective expectation of regret that may be experienced after a future action, inaction, or outcome.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Anticipated regret can enter decision evaluation before the outcome occurs and is distinct from experienced regret.
failure_modes: Using regret language as proof of actual anticipated regret
Assuming regret appeals always improve choices

nodes.label: Status Motivation
nodes.definition: Motivation to acquire, maintain, improve, or defend relative social standing within a relevant hierarchy.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Status motives can shape choice and signaling when social rank is psychologically relevant.
failure_modes: Treating all premium consumption as status motivation

nodes.label: Reputation Concern
nodes.definition: Concern about how one's character, competence, choices, or behavior are evaluated and remembered by others.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Reputation concerns can motivate impression-management and signaling behaviors under social observability.
failure_modes: Inferring reputation concern from public behavior alone

nodes.label: Interpersonal Liking
nodes.definition: Positive interpersonal evaluation or affect toward another person or source.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Liking can increase receptivity and compliance in some social-influence settings but remains distinct from trust, expertise, or evidence quality.
failure_modes: Equating liking with trustworthiness
Treating attractive design as interpersonal liking

nodes.label: Perceived Similarity
nodes.definition: Perception that another person or source shares relevant characteristics, experiences, values, beliefs, or identities.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Similarity can affect affiliation and source response, but effects depend on which dimension is similar and the active context.
failure_modes: Equating demographic similarity with psychological similarity
Equating similarity with in-group identification

nodes.label: Availability Heuristic
nodes.definition: Use of the accessibility or ease of retrieving examples or instances as information for judgment.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Accessible examples can influence judgment when accessibility is treated as diagnostic, but ecological validity depends on environment and task.
failure_modes: Treating memorability as objective frequency
Assuming availability always biases rather than sometimes informs

nodes.label: Choice Overload
nodes.definition: Adverse choice consequences that can arise from a large or complex assortment under particular decision conditions.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Overload is conditional on factors such as set complexity, task difficulty, preference uncertainty, and decision goals; assortment size alone is insufficient.
failure_modes: Using a fixed option-count threshold
Assuming fewer options are universally better

nodes.label: Asymmetric-Dominance / Decoy Effect
nodes.definition: Context-dependent preference shift toward a target option after adding an alternative that is dominated by the target but not equivalently by the competitor.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Choice sets can construct relative preference; decoy effects depend on attribute structure and task/context.
failure_modes: Adding an obviously bad option without asymmetric dominance and calling it a decoy
Assuming the effect is guaranteed

nodes.label: Present Bias
nodes.definition: Disproportionate preference for more immediate outcomes relative to later outcomes beyond constant exponential discounting.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Immediate outcomes can receive extra weight, producing preference reversals and time-inconsistent choices.
failure_modes: Equating all impatience with present bias
Assuming present bias is stable across domains

nodes.label: Evaluative Conditioning
nodes.definition: Change in evaluation of a target resulting from pairing it with positively or negatively valenced stimuli.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Pairings can change liking/evaluation, but effect magnitude and persistence depend on procedure, awareness, timing, and context.
failure_modes: Treating mere co-occurrence as guaranteed durable attitude change
Assuming laboratory effect transports directly to behavior

nodes.label: Personal Involvement / Message Relevance
nodes.definition: Degree to which a persuasive issue or message is personally consequential or relevant enough to motivate processing.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Greater involvement can alter elaboration and the relative influence of argument quality versus simpler source/context cues.
failure_modes: Equating involvement with attention duration
Assuming high involvement always increases persuasion

nodes.label: Counterarguing
nodes.definition: Generation or activation of issue-relevant thoughts that oppose, challenge, or rebut a persuasive message.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Counterarguing can reduce persuasion and participates in resistance/reactance processes.
failure_modes: Treating any negative sentiment as counterarguing

nodes.label: Inoculation / Prebunking
nodes.definition: Pre-exposure intervention that warns of a future persuasive challenge and/or provides weakened counterarguments with refutations to build resistance.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Inoculation can increase resistance to later persuasion, but mechanisms and timing moderators are not universally as originally theorized.
failure_modes: Treating any disclaimer as inoculation
Assuming threat/involvement always strengthen inoculation

nodes.label: Semantic Priming
nodes.definition: Facilitation or altered processing of a target due to prior activation of semantically related information.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Semantic relations can change lexical processing independently of simple associative co-occurrence, with task and relation-type moderators.
failure_modes: Equating priming with persuasion
Assuming all related words produce the same effect

nodes.label: Concreteness / Imageability
nodes.definition: Degree to which word/concept meaning refers to readily perceptible entities or evokes sensory imagery, with concreteness and imageability related but nonidentical.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Concrete language is often processed more efficiently, but lexical form, familiarity, context, and imageability contribute to observed effects.
failure_modes: Treating all concrete wording as clearer or more persuasive
Collapsing concreteness and imageability

nodes.label: Audience Design
nodes.definition: Adaptation of utterance form/content to properties, needs, or likely knowledge of an addressee.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Communicators can adapt through feedforward knowledge and recurrent prediction of communicative effects.
failure_modes: Overpersonalizing based on unsupported audience assumptions
Treating segmentation as proof of common ground

nodes.label: Perspective Taking in Communication
nodes.definition: Representation and use of another communicator's likely knowledge, viewpoint, or informational access during production or comprehension.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Perspective information can coordinate meaning, but people integrate it imperfectly with egocentric knowledge and context.
failure_modes: Assuming perfect theory-of-mind inference
Treating persona stereotypes as the audience's actual perspective

nodes.label: Character Identification
nodes.definition: Narrative process in which recipients adopt, experience, or align with a character's perspective, goals, or self-relevant position.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Identification can be strengthened by relevant similarity and can contribute to narrative persuasion alongside transportation.
failure_modes: Equating liking a character with identification
Assuming demographic similarity always increases identification

nodes.label: Primacy Ordering
nodes.definition: Message ordering in which earlier-presented information receives greater downstream influence than later information under specified conditions.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Primacy is a possible order effect, not a universal rule; involvement, delay, competing messages, and audience characteristics can alter or reverse it.
failure_modes: Always putting the 'strongest point first' because of a presumed universal primacy effect

nodes.label: Contrast Structure
nodes.definition: Deliberate rhetorical juxtaposition of alternatives, attributes, states, or outcomes to make differences cognitively and evaluatively salient.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Contrast can support comparative processing but can also create credibility or reactance costs depending on claims and context.
failure_modes: Using misleading comparisons
Assuming more contrast always means more persuasion

nodes.label: One-Sided Message
nodes.definition: Persuasive message structure that presents arguments supporting the advocated position without substantively presenting opposing considerations.
nodes.mechanism_summary: One-sidedness is a structural property whose effectiveness depends on audience knowledge/position, message context, and availability of counterarguments.
failure_modes: Treating one-sidedness as always less credible
Hiding material limitations where disclosure is required

nodes.label: Novelty Orienting
nodes.definition: Orienting of attention toward novel or expectancy-violating stimulation relative to the current context.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Novelty can alter attentional priority, but novelty is not identical to salience, surprise, curiosity, or sustained attention.
failure_modes: Do not infer Novelty Orienting directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Novelty Orienting as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Top-Down Attentional Selection
nodes.definition: Goal- or task-dependent prioritization of information for selection and processing.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Current goals bias selection among competing inputs, interacting with stimulus-driven and history-based influences.
failure_modes: Do not infer Top-Down Attentional Selection directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Top-Down Attentional Selection as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Feature-Based Attention
nodes.definition: Selective prioritization based on currently relevant stimulus features such as color, shape, category-linked cues, or other task-defined attributes.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Feature-based selection is one form of goal-directed attention and should not be inferred from post hoc engagement.
failure_modes: Do not infer Feature-Based Attention directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Feature-Based Attention as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Active Maintenance
nodes.definition: Temporary maintenance of task-relevant information in an accessible state for ongoing cognition.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Maintenance is a working-memory function distinct from capacity, updating, and long-term storage.
failure_modes: Do not infer Active Maintenance directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Active Maintenance as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Interference Susceptibility
nodes.definition: Degree to which competing information disrupts maintenance, selection, or use of task-relevant representations.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Interference can reduce effective working-memory performance without being identical to low capacity.
failure_modes: Do not infer Interference Susceptibility directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Interference Susceptibility as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Goal Discrepancy
nodes.definition: Perceived gap between a current state and a desired or goal state.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Discrepancy can energize goal pursuit when the goal matters and action seems viable, but large gaps may also discourage or redirect behavior.
failure_modes: Do not infer Goal Discrepancy directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Goal Discrepancy as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Goal Importance
nodes.definition: Perceived significance or priority of attaining a goal relative to other concerns.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Goal importance increases motivational relevance but does not guarantee commitment, persistence, or perceived attainability.
failure_modes: Do not infer Goal Importance directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Goal Importance as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Approach Motivation
nodes.definition: Motivational orientation toward moving toward, obtaining, engaging with, or attaining desired outcomes.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Approach motivation organizes direction of action and can occur with both positive and some negative emotions.
failure_modes: Do not infer Approach Motivation directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Approach Motivation as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Avoidance Motivation
nodes.definition: Motivational orientation toward preventing, escaping, distancing from, or reducing undesired outcomes.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Avoidance motivation is not equivalent to negative affect and can support active protective action.
failure_modes: Do not infer Avoidance Motivation directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Avoidance Motivation as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Goal Disengagement
nodes.definition: Reduction or withdrawal of commitment and effort from a goal that is abandoned, reprioritized, or judged unattainable/inappropriate.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Disengagement can be adaptive rather than simply motivational failure.
failure_modes: Do not infer Goal Disengagement directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Goal Disengagement as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Self-Verification
nodes.definition: Motivation to obtain or preserve feedback and interactions that are consistent with existing self-views.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Self-verification may compete with self-enhancement and is partly rooted in social-relational functioning.
failure_modes: Do not infer Self-Verification directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Self-Verification as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Self-Enhancement
nodes.definition: Motivation to maintain or increase favorable views of the self.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Self-enhancement is distinct from self-verification and should not be assumed to dominate every identity-relevant judgment.
failure_modes: Do not infer Self-Enhancement directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Self-Enhancement as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Identity Salience
nodes.definition: Degree to which a particular identity or group membership is cognitively active and relevant in the current context.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Membership alone does not establish salience; context determines which identity becomes influential.
failure_modes: Do not infer Identity Salience directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Identity Salience as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Perceived Authority Legitimacy
nodes.definition: Perceived legitimacy of a person's or institution's right to issue directives, requests, standards, or judgments in a relevant domain.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Authority effects depend on legitimacy and context; authority is not equivalent to expertise or truth.
failure_modes: Do not infer Perceived Authority Legitimacy directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Perceived Authority Legitimacy as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Social Exclusion Sensitivity
nodes.definition: Sensitivity to cues of rejection, ostracism, exclusion, or threatened belonging.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Exclusion cues can threaten relational needs and change subsequent social behavior, but not every negative social cue is exclusion.
failure_modes: Do not infer Social Exclusion Sensitivity directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Social Exclusion Sensitivity as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Representativeness Heuristic
nodes.definition: Use of similarity to a prototype, category, or generating process as a cue in judgment.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Representativeness can be useful or misleading depending on base rates, environment, and task structure.
failure_modes: Do not infer Representativeness Heuristic directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Representativeness Heuristic as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Ambiguity Aversion
nodes.definition: Preference to avoid options with poorly specified or unknown probabilities relative to options with better-specified probabilities, conditional on context.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Ambiguity aversion is distinct from risk aversion because the probability information itself differs in precision or availability.
failure_modes: Do not infer Ambiguity Aversion directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Ambiguity Aversion as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Opportunity-Cost Salience
nodes.definition: Accessibility of the value of forgone alternatives during evaluation of a focal choice.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Making opportunity costs salient can alter willingness to choose or buy, but consideration of opportunity cost can also increase discomfort or regret.
failure_modes: Do not infer Opportunity-Cost Salience directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Opportunity-Cost Salience as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Attribute Weighting
nodes.definition: Assignment of relative importance or decision weight to attributes when comparing options.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Weights can change with context, goals, framing, and trade-off structure rather than functioning as fixed universal preferences.
failure_modes: Do not infer Attribute Weighting directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Attribute Weighting as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Choice Conflict
nodes.definition: Experienced difficulty or tension when attractive or important considerations favor competing options or goals.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Conflict depends on trade-off structure and may produce delay, compromise, or other resolution strategies.
failure_modes: Do not infer Choice Conflict directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Choice Conflict as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Belief Strength
nodes.definition: Degree of conviction or endorsement attached to a proposition or belief.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Belief strength is distinct from attitude valence, confidence in one's thoughts, and objective truth.
failure_modes: Do not infer Belief Strength directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Belief Strength as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Attitude Valence
nodes.definition: Direction and degree of positive versus negative evaluation of an attitude object.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Valence alone does not capture certainty, accessibility, ambivalence, or behavioral consistency.
failure_modes: Do not infer Attitude Valence directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Attitude Valence as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Attitude Accessibility
nodes.definition: Ease or speed with which an attitude is activated from memory when the attitude object is encountered.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Accessibility is an attitude-strength property and should not be inferred solely from extremity or repeated exposure.
failure_modes: Do not infer Attitude Accessibility directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Attitude Accessibility as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Evidence Quality
nodes.definition: Perceived and/or normatively assessed quality of evidence offered in support of a claim.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Evidence quality is multidimensional; runtime must distinguish source credibility, diagnosticity, methodological quality, and logical relevance.
failure_modes: Do not infer Evidence Quality directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Evidence Quality as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires deeper construct/measurement validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Thought Confidence
nodes.definition: Confidence a person has in the validity or correctness of their own message-relevant thoughts.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Thought confidence validates whichever thoughts dominate: confidence in positive thoughts can increase persuasion, while confidence in negative thoughts can decrease it.
failure_modes: Do not infer Thought Confidence directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Thought Confidence as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Denotative Meaning
nodes.definition: Core conventional referential or conceptual content associated with a lexical expression in context.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Denotation does not exhaust pragmatic, connotative, affective, or discourse meaning.
failure_modes: Do not infer Denotative Meaning directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Denotative Meaning as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Connotative Meaning
nodes.definition: Associated evaluative, affective, social, or culturally learned meanings carried beyond narrow denotative content.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Connotation is context- and community-sensitive and should not be assumed universal across audiences.
failure_modes: Do not infer Connotative Meaning directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Connotative Meaning as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Syntactic Complexity
nodes.definition: Structural complexity of sentence syntax that can alter parsing and integration demands.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Syntactic complexity is one contributor to processing demand and cannot be reduced to sentence length.
failure_modes: Do not infer Syntactic Complexity directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Syntactic Complexity as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Conversational Implicature
nodes.definition: Context-dependent inferred meaning conveyed beyond what is explicitly encoded in the literal sentence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Implicatures are defeasible and depend on context, common ground, communicative assumptions, and alternatives.
failure_modes: Do not infer Conversational Implicature directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Conversational Implicature as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Local Discourse Coherence
nodes.definition: Degree to which adjacent or nearby discourse units form interpretable semantic/pragmatic relations that support a connected representation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Local coherence supports comprehension but is distinct from global discourse organization and factual consistency.
failure_modes: Do not infer Local Discourse Coherence directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Local Discourse Coherence as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Premise Support
nodes.definition: Degree to which reasons or premises offered in a message provide relevant support for the advocated claim.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Premise support is an argument-design property; receiver-side acceptance and argument quality remain separate C5 processes.
failure_modes: Do not infer Premise Support directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Premise Support as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires deeper construct/measurement validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Evidence–Claim Linkage
nodes.definition: Explicitness and defensibility of the inferential link between presented evidence and the claim it is intended to support.
nodes.mechanism_summary: A strong-looking evidence block does not support a claim if the inferential linkage is weak or mismatched.
failure_modes: Do not infer Evidence–Claim Linkage directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Evidence–Claim Linkage as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires deeper construct/measurement validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Argument Warrant
nodes.definition: Rule, assumption, or inferential bridge that licenses movement from premises/evidence to a conclusion.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Warrants can be implicit; this node is retained as a rhetoric/argumentation design construct pending deeper argumentation-science evidence.
failure_modes: Do not infer Argument Warrant directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Argument Warrant as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires deeper construct/measurement validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Narrative Coherence
nodes.definition: Degree to which narrative events, goals, causal relations, and character actions form an intelligible and connected story representation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Narrative coherence supports narrative processing but is not equivalent to transportation or identification.
failure_modes: Do not infer Narrative Coherence directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Narrative Coherence as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Analogy / Cross-Domain Mapping
nodes.definition: Deliberate mapping of relational structure from a source domain to a target concept to aid explanation, organization, or persuasion.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Metaphor evidence suggests small context-dependent persuasive advantages, but analogy is broader than metaphor and remains provisional as a separate copywriting design node.
failure_modes: Do not infer Analogy / Cross-Domain Mapping directly from a single platform metric or copy outcome.
Do not treat Analogy / Cross-Domain Mapping as a universal effect independent of context and boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires deeper construct/measurement validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Abrupt-Onset Attentional Priority
nodes.definition: Priority advantage that can occur when a new stimulus appears abruptly within an ongoing perceptual context.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Abrupt onset can attract selection under some task conditions, but onset is not a universal guarantee of capture.
failure_modes: Do not infer Abrupt-Onset Attentional Priority from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Abrupt-Onset Attentional Priority as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Distractor-Capture Susceptibility
nodes.definition: Tendency for task-irrelevant but salient or otherwise prioritized stimuli to interfere with target-directed selection.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Observed distraction reflects interaction among salience, goals, selection history and control; a stable susceptibility trait should not be assumed without appropriate measurement.
failure_modes: Do not infer Distractor-Capture Susceptibility from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Distractor-Capture Susceptibility as a universal copywriting rule without context.
open_questions: Requires narrower evidence or transport validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Spatial Attentional Selection
nodes.definition: Selective allocation of attentional priority to a location or spatial region.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Spatial selection is one component of attention and should not be conflated with feature- or object-based selection.
failure_modes: Do not infer Spatial Attentional Selection from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Spatial Attentional Selection as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Processing Disfluency
nodes.definition: Experienced difficulty or reduced ease in processing a stimulus relative to a fluent baseline.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Disfluency can alter judgment and processing strategy, but difficult-to-process information is not automatically more memorable, truthful, or deeply processed.
failure_modes: Do not infer Processing Disfluency from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Processing Disfluency as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Retrieval-Cue Effectiveness
nodes.definition: Degree to which available cues support access to previously encoded information.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Retrieval success depends on cue-memory relation and context; failure to recall does not prove absence of encoding.
failure_modes: Do not infer Retrieval-Cue Effectiveness from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Retrieval-Cue Effectiveness as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Habituation
nodes.definition: Reduction in orienting or response to repeated or continuously presented stimulation when it becomes less informative or novel.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Repeated exposure can reduce orienting, but habituation is not equivalent to boredom, dislike, or memory loss.
failure_modes: Do not infer Habituation from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Habituation as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Need Activation
nodes.definition: Increase in motivational relevance of a need or concern such that related goals and outcomes become more behaviorally significant.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Activated needs can organize valuation and goal pursuit, but need labels should not be inferred directly from a copy response.
failure_modes: Do not infer Need Activation from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Need Activation as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Reward Anticipation
nodes.definition: Prospective representation of expected rewarding outcomes before they are experienced.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Anticipated reward contributes to motivation and value but is distinct from experienced reward and from incentive salience.
failure_modes: Do not infer Reward Anticipation from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Reward Anticipation as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Perceived Motivational Cost
nodes.definition: Subjective effort, time, emotional, opportunity, or other cost expected from pursuing a task or goal.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Costs can reduce motivation even when value and expectancy are high, and effort can sometimes itself acquire value.
failure_modes: Do not infer Perceived Motivational Cost from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Perceived Motivational Cost as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Valence Appraisal
nodes.definition: Appraisal of whether an event or outcome is favorable versus unfavorable relative to goals or well-being.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Valence appraisal contributes to emotion but cannot identify a specific discrete emotion on its own.
failure_modes: Do not infer Valence Appraisal from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Valence Appraisal as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Emotion Differentiation
nodes.definition: Differentiation of affective experience into distinct emotional states based on appraisal patterns and other components.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Different emotions with similar valence can produce different action tendencies and judgments.
failure_modes: Do not infer Emotion Differentiation from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Emotion Differentiation as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Action Readiness
nodes.definition: State of preparedness to act in response to an appraised event, goal, or opportunity.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Action readiness is broader than any one approach/avoidance direction and does not guarantee observed action.
failure_modes: Do not infer Action Readiness from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Action Readiness as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Self-Schema Activation
nodes.definition: Activation of organized self-relevant knowledge that guides interpretation of information in relation to the self.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Self-schema activation can change what feels personally diagnostic or relevant, but not all self-reference implies a stable schema.
failure_modes: Do not infer Self-Schema Activation from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Self-Schema Activation as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Aspirational Identity / Desired Self
nodes.definition: Representation of a desired, possible, or idealized self-state that can create discrepancy with the current self and motivate symbolic or direct regulation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Products and messages may acquire psychological value when linked to self-discrepancy reduction, but aspirational identity is not automatically status motivation.
failure_modes: Do not infer Aspirational Identity / Desired Self from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Aspirational Identity / Desired Self as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Conformity Pressure
nodes.definition: Social pressure to align judgments or behavior with group expectations, norms, or perceived consensus.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Conformity can reflect normative or informational influence and should not be reduced to popularity alone.
failure_modes: Do not infer Conformity Pressure from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Conformity Pressure as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Norm Internalization
nodes.definition: Process by which a social norm becomes personally endorsed or integrated rather than followed only because of external pressure.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Internalized norms differ from surface compliance and can persist without immediate monitoring.
failure_modes: Do not infer Norm Internalization from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Norm Internalization as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Identity Signaling
nodes.definition: Use of choices, expressions, or behaviors to communicate identity-relevant information to others or to reinforce self-concept.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Identity signaling overlaps impression management, status signaling, and self-expression; exact boundaries remain context-dependent.
failure_modes: Do not infer Identity Signaling from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Identity Signaling as a universal copywriting rule without context.
open_questions: Requires narrower evidence or transport validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Homophily Cue
nodes.definition: Cue suggesting similarity or shared characteristics between a source and recipient that can influence affiliation or source evaluation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Homophily effects vary by similarity dimension and context; similarity does not guarantee trust or persuasion.
failure_modes: Do not infer Homophily Cue from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Homophily Cue as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Affect Heuristic
nodes.definition: Use of immediate affective response as information or a simplifying cue in judgment.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Affect can simplify judgment but its diagnosticity depends on whether the feeling is relevant to the target decision.
failure_modes: Do not infer Affect Heuristic from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Affect Heuristic as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Gain–Loss Framing
nodes.definition: Change in evaluation or choice produced by describing substantively related outcomes in gain versus loss terms relative to a reference representation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Framing effects depend on reference point, domain, and task; wording alone does not imply a prospect-theory mechanism.
failure_modes: Do not infer Gain–Loss Framing from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Gain–Loss Framing as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Mental Accounting
nodes.definition: Cognitive categorization and evaluation of economic outcomes within partially segregated mental accounts rather than treating all resources as fully fungible.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Mental accounting can shape spending and choice, but account boundaries are context-dependent rather than objectively fixed.
failure_modes: Do not infer Mental Accounting from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Mental Accounting as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Probability Weighting
nodes.definition: Nonlinear transformation or weighting of objective/subjective probabilities in risky choice.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Probability-dependent preferences can differ from linear expected-value treatment and appear in both laboratory and real-world risk behavior.
failure_modes: Do not infer Probability Weighting from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Probability Weighting as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Probability Calibration
nodes.definition: Degree of correspondence between expressed confidence/probability judgments and observed frequencies or outcomes across an appropriate set of predictions.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Calibration is a property of judgments over cases and is distinct from confidence magnitude in a single decision.
failure_modes: Do not infer Probability Calibration from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Probability Calibration as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Delay Aversion
nodes.definition: Negative valuation or motivational cost specifically associated with waiting or delayed receipt beyond general temporal discounting.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Delay aversion may contribute to intertemporal choice but requires distinction from present bias, opportunity cost, and general impatience.
failure_modes: Do not infer Delay Aversion from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Delay Aversion as a universal copywriting rule without context.
open_questions: Requires narrower evidence or transport validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Elaboration Likelihood
nodes.definition: Likelihood or degree that a recipient engages in effortful issue-relevant thinking about a persuasive communication.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Elaboration depends on motivation and ability; it is a continuum of processing rather than a fixed audience type.
failure_modes: Do not infer Elaboration Likelihood from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Elaboration Likelihood as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Systematic / Central Processing
nodes.definition: Relatively effortful evaluation of message content, arguments, implications, and evidence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: More systematic processing increases sensitivity to argument quality but does not guarantee agreement.
failure_modes: Do not infer Systematic / Central Processing from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Systematic / Central Processing as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Heuristic / Peripheral Processing
nodes.definition: Use of simpler cues, learned rules, or low-effort information when forming or changing judgments under limited elaboration.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Heuristic cues can also bias more systematic processing; the processes are not strictly mutually exclusive.
failure_modes: Do not infer Heuristic / Peripheral Processing from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Heuristic / Peripheral Processing as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Evidence Diagnosticity
nodes.definition: Perceived degree to which a piece of evidence discriminates among competing hypotheses or claims and therefore bears on the decision at hand.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Evidence can be credible yet weakly diagnostic for the specific claim; diagnosticity is claim-relative.
failure_modes: Do not infer Evidence Diagnosticity from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Evidence Diagnosticity as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Self-Validation
nodes.definition: Process by which confidence or other metacognitive cues change how much a person relies on their own thoughts when forming an attitude.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Self-validation magnifies the influence of whichever thoughts dominate, rather than simply increasing persuasion.
failure_modes: Do not infer Self-Validation from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Self-Validation as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Behavioral Intention
nodes.definition: Self-reported or inferred readiness/plan to perform a specified future behavior.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Intention is a proximal psychological outcome and must remain distinct from observed behavior.
failure_modes: Do not infer Behavioral Intention from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Behavioral Intention as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Syntactic Ambiguity
nodes.definition: Presence of more than one plausible syntactic parse or structural interpretation for an expression.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Ambiguity can increase processing/revision demands and is resolved using structural, lexical, semantic, and discourse information.
failure_modes: Do not infer Syntactic Ambiguity from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Syntactic Ambiguity as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Dependency Length
nodes.definition: Linear distance between syntactically dependent words or constituents.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Longer dependencies generally increase memory/processing pressure and languages show strong pressures toward dependency-length minimization.
failure_modes: Do not infer Dependency Length from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Dependency Length as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Deictic / Reference Interpretation
nodes.definition: Resolution of expressions whose referent depends on discourse, speaker, location, time, or shared context.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Reference interpretation relies on context and common ground rather than lexical content alone.
failure_modes: Do not infer Deictic / Reference Interpretation from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Deictic / Reference Interpretation as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Scalar Implicature
nodes.definition: Inference in which use of a weaker scalar expression can imply that a stronger alternative does not hold, such as interpreting 'some' as 'some but not all'.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Scalar inference depends on alternatives, grammar/pragmatics, context, and processing conditions rather than arising as an invariant automatic rule.
failure_modes: Do not infer Scalar Implicature from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Scalar Implicature as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Ambiguity Resolution
