nodes.definition: Process of selecting or revising among competing lexical, syntactic, or referential interpretations using contextual and linguistic evidence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Resolution is incremental and can require reanalysis when early interpretations prove inconsistent.
failure_modes: Do not infer Ambiguity Resolution from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Ambiguity Resolution as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Global Discourse Coherence
nodes.definition: Degree to which discourse as a whole supports a connected, interpretable representation across larger spans and overarching goals/topics.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Global coherence is distinct from local adjacency relations and can depend on inferred goals, themes, and world knowledge.
failure_modes: Do not infer Global Discourse Coherence from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Global Discourse Coherence as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Argument Completeness
nodes.definition: Degree to which a message provides the components and support needed for its central argumentative move without leaving critical inferential gaps.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Completeness is audience- and claim-dependent and does not guarantee truth or persuasion.
failure_modes: Do not infer Argument Completeness from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Argument Completeness as a universal copywriting rule without context.
open_questions: Requires narrower evidence or transport validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Ethos Appeal
nodes.definition: Rhetorical strategy that foregrounds the character, credibility, authority, values, or persona of a speaker/source.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Ethos is a rhetorical design category; receiver-side credibility judgments belong in C5 and must not be collapsed with the appeal itself.
failure_modes: Do not infer Ethos Appeal from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Ethos Appeal as a universal copywriting rule without context.
open_questions: Requires narrower evidence or transport validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Logos Appeal
nodes.definition: Rhetorical strategy that foregrounds reasons, evidence, logical relations, causal explanation, or argument structure.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Logos is a rhetorical category rather than a single cognitive mechanism; effects depend on argument quality and elaboration.
failure_modes: Do not infer Logos Appeal from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Logos Appeal as a universal copywriting rule without context.
open_questions: Requires narrower evidence or transport validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Causal Narrative Structure
nodes.definition: Narrative organization in which events are connected through causal relations, goals, consequences, and temporal progression.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Causal structure contributes to narrative coherence and situation-model construction, but it is not sufficient by itself for transportation.
failure_modes: Do not infer Causal Narrative Structure from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Causal Narrative Structure as a universal copywriting rule without context.

nodes.label: Recency Ordering
nodes.definition: Message ordering in which later-presented information exerts greater downstream influence than earlier information under specified conditions.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Recency competes with primacy and other order effects; no universal last-position rule is accepted.
failure_modes: Do not infer Recency Ordering from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Recency Ordering as a universal copywriting rule without context.
open_questions: Requires narrower evidence or transport validation before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Before–After Structure
nodes.definition: Comparative rhetorical structure that contrasts a prior/current state with a later/desired state to foreground change or transformation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: This is a useful copy-design pattern, but its psychological effect depends on the underlying contrast, evidence, goals, and narrative mechanisms rather than the label itself.
failure_modes: Do not infer Before–After Structure from a single outcome metric.
Do not apply Before–After Structure as a universal copywriting rule without context.
open_questions: Requires narrower evidence or transport validation before strong runtime use.
